rationale: Both candidates independently converge on the ground-truth's central theme (the `!= "cpu"` widening breaks the intended CUDA/MUSA-only allowlist and risks NPU/XPU) and both flag the same FL2VA/Ref2VA doc copy-paste bug and missing test coverage for the new branch. X goes further with a technically sound, code-grounded catch that Y misses entirely: `torch.random.fork_rng` resolves its save/restore module from the `device_type` kwarg (default "cuda"), not from the `devices` list, so passing a MUSA device without `device_type="musa"` silently saves/restores the wrong RNG — a real correctness bug with a concrete one-line fix. X also flags the device_module being resolved once at construction via the global accelerator rather than per-parameter. Y's unique findings (torch version pin, audio-path claim) are weaker and more tangential to the actual diff. X's fixes are consistently more concrete (inline diffs) making it the stronger review overall.
